question: Does a summed-writer compiler trained in the broader Tomorrow/Earlier reader mode predict Later/Previously responses, reversing the failed narrow-to-broad transfer?

authority.cross_cue_terminal: shared_mode with asymmetric original-to-fresh oracle response transfer

novelty: The frozen forward compiler trained on Later/Previously failed causal OOD transfer. The factorial then found that Tomorrow/Earlier reader axes transfer in the reverse direction. No coefficient compiler has tested that prospective asymmetry.

frozen_design.fit: balanced 16-row Tomorrow/Earlier A1 lexical subset with eight rows per orientation
frozen_design.test: all 32 Later/Previously A1, 32 A2, and 32 aligned P rows
frozen_design.compiler: one summed writer SVD coefficient, two reader rank-one axes, and two affine coefficient maps (four scalars), all fitted only on Tomorrow/Earlier

predictions.pred_a_capability_and_writer_closure: all answer-changing test rows natively correct and exact writer reconstruction <=1e-4 on fit/A1/A2/P
predictions.pred_b_reverse_coefficient_prediction: both reader coefficient correlations absolute r>=0.60 on fresh A1 and A2
predictions.pred_c_reverse_program_material: predicted program retains >=0.60 of full response and is donorward on >=0.75 of fresh A1/A2 rows
predictions.pred_d_prediction_beats_intercept: predicted recovery exceeds intercept-only by >=0.15 of full response on A1/A2
predictions.pred_f_price_exact: 38 forwards, 1104 examples, 320 records, four scalars, 512 axes, zero backwards/updates

terminal_rules.invalid: authority, capability, alignment, closure, coverage, finiteness, or price fails
terminal_rules.coefficient_asymmetry: oracle broad mode is material but predicted coefficients fail
terminal_rules.response_asymmetry: even oracle broad mode is not material on the test corpus

interpretation_limits: A pass selects a canonical basis across these two cue lexicons, not universal temporal language.
The exact block8H1 source terms remain native inputs to the compiler.
C selectivity remains inherited because C lacks aligned writer semantics.
